transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I came in because I can’t make myself go near the front windows or that part of the street anymore. At work, I keep finding excuses to stay in the back, even though being out front is part of my job.
Did something traumatic happen near those front windows or on that part of the street?
I… I can’t really go near that area anymore. The front windows and that stretch of street make me want to stay in the back, even though I’m supposed to work out front.
Did something happen there that felt traumatic or terrifying to you?
I’m not sure. I just know I really don’t want to be near that spot.
When you get near the front windows or that part of the street, do unwanted memories of something frightening pop into your mind?
Yeah. The crash just pops into my head, especially when I’m setting up displays. I suddenly hear the bang and see the glass coming down, like it’s happening all over again.
Were you ever physically present when that crash happened?
I’m… I’m not sure. I know I remember it really clearly, but I don’t know if I was actually there when it happened.
Were you there when the crash happened?
I honestly can’t tell. It feels so real in my head, but I don’t know if I was actually there.
When you think about going near the front windows or that part of the street, are you mainly afraid that you’ll panic or lose control in front of other people?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed being afraid of panicking in front of people.
When you avoid the front windows, is it because being there brings back the crash?
Yeah. Being near the front windows—or that part of the street—just brings it all back. I keep making excuses to stay in the back, even though I’m supposed to be out there.
Do you avoid the front windows because you think that area is dangerous?
I don’t know if I think it’s dangerous exactly. I just can’t make myself go near it. I keep finding reasons to stay in the back instead, even though I’m supposed to be out front for work.
Were you there in person when the crash happened?
I—I’m not sure what you mean. I know being near the windows brings it back, but I haven’t really talked through whether I was there when it happened.
Did you personally witness the crash happen?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been able to sort out that part of it.
Besides that spot by the front windows, are there other places like streets or windows that you also avoid?
Mostly the front windows and that part of the street. I just avoid going out there if I can, and I keep making excuses to stay in the back at work.
When you think about going near the front windows or that part of the street, are you afraid you wouldn’t be able to get away or get help if something happened?
I don’t know if it’s about not being able to get away or get help. I just know I don’t want to be near there.
At the time of the crash, were you physically there and saw it happen with your own eyes?
I honestly can’t tell. That part is still really unclear to me.
Do you also avoid other public places, like stores or public transportation?
It’s mostly those front windows and that stretch of street. At work I keep trying to stay in the back instead of going up there, even though I’m supposed to.
Do you avoid other streets because they remind you of the crash?
Not really other streets. It’s that particular stretch by the front windows—I just can’t make myself go near it. I keep finding reasons to stay in the back at work instead.
Are you specifically afraid of the front windows themselves?
Not the windows themselves exactly. It’s being near them, and that part of the street. I just can’t make myself go up there, so I keep finding excuses to stay in the back.
If that front part of the store were changed completely so it no longer reminded you of the crash, would you still be afraid to go there?
I think I’d still have trouble with it. I can’t make myself go near that front area, and I keep avoiding it by staying in the back, even though I’m supposed to be up there sometimes.
When you go near that front area, does it make you relive the crash?
Yeah. Especially when I’m trying to set up displays, it just pops into my head. I can hear the bang and see the glass coming down—it feels like it’s happening again for a second.
Did you actually experience the crash yourself?
I’m not sure what you mean by “actually experienced.” I know being near that area brings it all back really strongly.
